title: Multitasking
coreMove: Stop treating attention switching as extra capacity and return to one consequential task at a time.
sourcePressure: This lie chapter rejects multitasking as false productivity, focusing on divided attention, switching, error risk, and the prestige of appearing busy on several fronts.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Saying phones are distracting or that people should generally focus more.

hook: A single choice changes the whole day
The real priority is hiding under the busy work
Multitasking as a generic focus opener
counterintuition: Focus is harder than it looks
tryThisNow: Set a timer and list priorities
Write down your one thing without a concrete context
examples: generic office worker choosing email or strategy

exampleSpecs.stakes: a pediatric dose has no margin for transcription error
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she places the ringing phone in a drawer and completes the dilution calculation before touching the refill queue
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a laminated dosing chart under one gloved finger beside a muted phone

exampleSpecs.stakes: the sponsor read must hit while breaking news updates arrive
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he locks the news chat, rides the sponsor timing cleanly, then returns to updates after the segment closes
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a red on-air light reflected in a glass mixing board

exampleSpecs.stakes: two allergy tickets and six normal orders hit at once
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she calls one allergy ticket at a time, turns the duplicate shouting into a sequence, and stops the garnish mistake before it happens
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two allergy tickets clipped apart above a sizzling expo line

exampleSpecs.domain: crane operator on a bridge repair
exampleSpecs.stakes: a steel beam swings above traffic
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the foreman cuts the budget call mid-sentence and keeps every signal on the beam until it lands on the bearing pad
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a suspended steel beam hanging over stopped traffic cones

exampleSpecs.stakes: one missed word changes a transcript
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she catches that checking exhibit numbers while typing caused the transcript gap and creates a strict handoff sequence
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a stenotype machine beside an exhibit sticker half-peeled from a folder

exampleSpecs.stakes: a reef tank crash could spread by morning
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she predicts answering donor texts during nitrate testing will be harmless, then catches the mislabeled vial before repeating the split
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two test vials with similar blue caps under fluorescent light

tryThisNowSpec: During your next important task, remove the second active task from the surface in front of you and write the reentry cost you avoided.
